campaigns.name: One Page. Every Deal.
campaigns.objective: awareness — put dealpage in front of founders who are actively outgrowing Notion or spreadsheets for pipeline tracking
campaigns.big_idea: Launch on Product Hunt with a demo that shows the entire pipeline living on one keyboard-navigable page. The hook is the contrast: founders already know what a bloated CRM feels like. Show them what it looks like when it isn't.
campaigns.hook: Your pipeline on one page. Your hands never leave the keyboard.

sample_copy.headline: One page. Every deal. No mouse required.
sample_copy.body: dealpage is a CRM built for founders doing their own sales. Move deals, log notes, and send synced email — all from the keyboard, all in under 100ms. No pipelines to configure. No admin console. Founders at 40 companies already use it as their primary CRM. 14-day free trial, no card required.

assets_needed: Product Hunt listing with GIF or short screen recording showing keyboard navigation
3-5 X posts scheduled around launch day
A short written maker comment explaining why dealpage exists
campaigns.success_metric: Number of trial signups on launch day
campaigns.why_on_brand: Mirrors the DNA's direct, second-person declaratives and grounds the claim in the published p95 latency proof point rather than vague superlatives.

campaigns.name: Show HN: CRM That Fits on One Page
campaigns.objective: signups — reach technical founders and early engineers on Hacker News who distrust bloated SaaS
campaigns.big_idea: A Show HN post written founder-to-founder, explaining the infrastructure decision to build keyboard-first and publish latency numbers. The technical specifics (TypeScript, Next.js, p95 under 100ms) are the credibility. No marketing language.
campaigns.hook: Show HN: I built a CRM for founders — the whole pipeline fits on one keyboard-driven page

sample_copy.headline: Show HN: dealpage — founder CRM, one page, keyboard-first, p95 under 100ms
sample_copy.body: HubSpot is built for sales ops teams. Founders end up in Notion. I built dealpage to sit between those two: a single keyboard-navigable page for your pipeline, notes, and two-way Gmail sync. No required fields, no workflow config. Imports from HubSpot or Pipedrive in minutes. p95 interaction latency is under 100ms — measured and published. Happy to share the architecture decisions.
sample_copy.cta: Try it free for 14 days — dealpage.com

assets_needed: Published latency benchmark page to link to
Prepared responses to likely HN questions (architecture, pricing, roadmap)
campaigns.success_metric: Number of trial signups from HN referral traffic within 72 hours
campaigns.why_on_brand: Transparent, pragmatic, grounded in specifics — matches the DNA's instruction to ground claims in measurable facts and speak directly to the reader's role.

campaigns.name: Migrated in an Afternoon
campaigns.objective: signups — convert founders currently on HubSpot or Pipedrive who feel the admin overhead
campaigns.big_idea: A short Reddit post in r/startups and r/entrepreneur framed as a founder sharing what they learned switching CRMs. The proof point — 12,000 contacts migrated out of HubSpot in one afternoon — does the work. No pitch, just the story.
campaigns.hook: We migrated 12,000 contacts out of HubSpot in one afternoon. Here's what we switched to and why.

sample_copy.headline: Migrated 12,000 contacts out of HubSpot in one afternoon
sample_copy.body: HubSpot is built for sales ops teams, not founders doing their own sales. We were spending more time configuring workflows than talking to customers. Switched to dealpage: one keyboard-navigable page, two-way Gmail sync, no admin console. The import took an afternoon. If you're a founder tracking deals in Notion because real CRMs feel like ERP software, worth a look.

assets_needed: Prepared follow-up comments answering likely questions about migration and pricing
campaigns.success_metric: Click-through rate from Reddit post to trial signup page
campaigns.why_on_brand: Uses the site's own customer proof point verbatim, written in plain second-person language with no hype — consistent with the DNA's avoid list and do list.

campaigns.name: Founder-to-Founder on X
campaigns.objective: community — build an audience of early-stage founders by sharing transparent, opinionated takes on CRM and founder sales
campaigns.big_idea: A recurring thread series on X where the builder shares specific, opinionated observations about how founders actually run sales — not best practices, but real patterns. Each thread ends with a natural mention of dealpage. The mechanic is consistency and specificity, not promotion.
campaigns.hook: Most founders track deals in Notion until it breaks. Here's what that moment looks like — and what to do about it.

sample_copy.body: You're mid-fundraise or hiring your first sales rep. Your Notion table has 80 rows and no one can read it. That's the moment. You don't need Salesforce. You need a pipeline on one page, keyboard-navigable, with Gmail sync that actually works. That's what we built. Direct, fast, no configuration required.

campaigns.success_metric: Follower growth and click-through to trial page over 6 weeks

campaigns.name: Latency as a Feature
campaigns.objective: signups — convert technically-minded founders who care about tool quality by making the p95 latency claim the centerpiece of a LinkedIn post
campaigns.big_idea: A single LinkedIn post written by the founder explaining why they measured and published interaction latency for a CRM — and what that decision says about how they think about software quality. The argument: if your tools are slow, your sales process is slow. The proof point is already published.
campaigns.hook: We measured and published the p95 interaction latency for our CRM. Here's why that matters for founders doing their own sales.

sample_copy.headline: We published our latency numbers. Here's why.
sample_copy.body: Most CRMs are built for sales ops teams with time to configure workflows. We built dealpage for founders who need to move fast. Every action lands in under 100ms — p95, measured, published. Not a marketing claim. A number you can check. If your pipeline tool is slow, your sales process is slow. One page. Keyboard-first. Two-way Gmail sync. 14-day free trial.
sample_copy.cta: Read the numbers and try it free at dealpage.com

assets_needed: Link to published latency benchmark page
Optional: simple chart or screenshot of the latency data
campaigns.success_metric: LinkedIn post impressions and trial signups from LinkedIn referral traffic
campaigns.why_on_brand: Transparent and pragmatic — grounds the claim in a published, verifiable number rather than a vague superlative, exactly as the DNA instructs.

confidence.notes: Campaigns are built on dealpage APP_PROFILE proof points (40 companies, 12,000 contacts, p95 latency) and Cal.com DNA voice patterns. The BRAND_DNA is Cal.com's, not dealpage's — campaigns adapt the DNA's direct/transparent/pragmatic voice to dealpage's product and ICP. No numeric claims were invented; all figures come from APP_PROFILE.proof_points. Channel selection prioritizes founder-heavy communities (HN, Reddit r/startups, X, LinkedIn, newsletters) consistent with the ICP.
